item.title: Mendi-Munihu district distributes rice to communities
item.description: The Mendi-Munihu District Development Authority (MMDDA) has distributed rice bags to families hard-hit by the ongoing El Niño drought that has left many households facing severe food shortages. Mendi-Munihu District Administrator Philip Koka confirmed the distribution, stating that the district used K2.5 million in relief funding provided by the National Government.
item.content:encoded:
The Mendi-Munihu District Development Authority (MMDDA) has distributed rice bags to families hard-hit by the ongoing El Niño drought that has left many households facing severe food shortages.

Mendi-Munihu District Administrator Philip Koka confirmed the distribution, stating that the district used K2.5 million in relief funding provided by the National Government.

Seven Hino trucks loaded with food supplies arrived at the Mendi-Munihu District Office at Six Mile, Tente, with supplies officially distributed to communities in the Upper Mendi Local Level Government (LLG) — making them the first communities in the district to receive the much-needed assistance. After Upper Mendi, Karinz LLG distributed its share and today Lai Valley LLG is distributing its share.

Lai Valley LLG President Manuel Olpa acknowledged the Mendi-Munihu DDA under the leadership of MP Raphael Tonpi for looking into the poor people's need and distributing rice to address the El Niño-induced food shortage.

"But for the ordinary people, the reality is very different. Some will say a bag of rice is not enough — and that may be true. But there are very poor families, families whose gardens and crops have completely failed due to the El Niño drought, who deeply appreciate this effort.

“For them, this rice is not just food, it is hope. It is the difference between going to bed hungry and feeding their children for another day," President Olpa said.

District CEO Mr Koka said while other basic food items were not included in this first round of rice bags, responding to the people's plea for help was critical as many families had gone hungry.

"Addressing the people's plea for help is important. In the second round, the Mendi-Munihu DDA can look at other food items as well. For now, this is from the immediate assistance funding given by the National Government which the MMDDA used to purchase them" Koka said.

The distribution was led by Upper Mendi LLG President Kevin Sapul, together with Karinz LLG President Simon Tolpe and Lai Valley President Manuel Olpa.

item.title: Wau Waria identifies more than sixty-three thousand El Nino victims

item.content:encoded:
Morobe’s Waria district is a step closer to accessing its K2.5 million El Nino relief fund allocation, after completing comprehensive drought assessments across all 43 wards, identifying 63,756 affected people from 14,394 households.

The findings by the District's El Nino Response Committee across the Wau Urban, Wau Rural and the Waria LLGs revealed widespread drinking water shortages, food insecurity, crop losses and health risks, providing the critical evidence needed to justify the release and utilisation of the funds.

The Wau Waria MP, as the District Development Authority (DDA) Chairman, Marsh Narewec clarified, that although the allocation is accessible, payments cannot be made without meeting the necessary accountability requirements.

"The K2.5 million is accessible but not accessed yet due to these assessments. We have to submit the assessment report to justify the release of payments. It is not a Tucker box where we hand out cash or make payments anyhow," he said.

Rather than waiting for the funds, the district's multi-stakeholder response committee has completed the assessments and is now finalising plans for distribution of the essential relief supplies, prioritising communities who were most affected.

The MP has so far acknowledged the collective efforts of the ward councillors, the LLG officers, the assessment teams and communities in completing this important part of the district-wide assessment.

Submission of the assessment report and fulfilment of the remaining requirements are now the final critical steps, towards accessing the K2.5 million needed to deliver the much-needed relief supplies.

item.title: Retired Major general calls for urgent intervention into law-and-order concerns
item.description: A former Commander of the PNG Defence Force has raised serious concerns about the law-and-order situation in the country, warning that it is eroding public confidence. Retired Major general Jerry Singirok says the growing violence calls for urgent government intervention.
item.content:encoded:
A former Commander of the PNG Defence Force has raised serious concerns about the law-and-order situation in the country, warning that it is eroding public confidence.

Retired Major general Jerry Singirok says the growing violence calls for urgent government intervention.

The increasing incidents of killings in settlements, ethnic clashes, armed robberies and other criminal activities in Port Moresby and other parts of the country have raised serious concerns about the effectiveness of the nation’s security and law enforcement agencies.

Retired Major general Jerry Singirok says the worsening security situation is not simply a law-and-order issue.

He describes it as a national development, economic and governance challenge.

"This has put a lot of strain on our government agencies but that doesn't give us as a responsible government an agency's excuse to allow escalation of and the deterioration of social conditions.

"I came out with my concern as former commander and a leader of this country to highlight this aspect of the challenges that we're facing. We need leaders at all levels. We need government departments that measure up to the expectation to fulfill their roles and duties." Singirok said.

Singirok says no nation can attract investment, create employment opportunities and improve living standard, when public safety is compromised.

The former Commander stressed that bold leadership, institutional competency and strong political will are essential to restoring public confidence and ensuring that the rule of law prevails.

"I have called on the government to take responsible actions; to assist in funding, technical advice, leadership and put our security forces under scrutiny so that they perform." Singirok said.

item.title: Goroka LLG boosts services amid growing demand
item.description: The Goroka Urban Local-Level Government LLG has acquired five new vehicles to strengthen its operations and improve service delivery across the town. Goroka’s growing population has increased pressure on the Urban LLG to deliver essential services, particularly water supply and rubbish collection to meet the rising demand.
item.content:encoded:
The Goroka Urban Local-Level Government LLG has acquired five new vehicles to strengthen its operations and improve service delivery across the town.

Goroka’s growing population has increased pressure on the Urban LLG to deliver essential services, particularly water supply and rubbish collection to meet the rising demand.

Town Manager Harold Abori says the new fleet will help the LLG respond to the growing workload and maintain essential services.

“All the money that we’ve collected from water rates, land rates and spot fines was saved, and we saw the need for more vehicles to support our operations.” Abori said.

The new fleet includes a six-ton dump truck and four Isuzu D-Max vehicles, allocated to different sectors to support their daily operations.

Goroka LLG truck driver Brenson Komboli says the growing population has increased rubbish across the town, putting additional pressure on waste collection services.

Mr Komboli says despite the four existing rubbish trucks making four collection rounds daily, they are still unable to clear all the rubbish generated across town.

“Rubbish is a big issue in Goroka. We urge people to dispose of their rubbish at the right places, but they continue to ignore the awareness we provide,” he says.

He says the shortage of vehicles previously forced rubbish collection workers to collect rubbish manually and pile it at designated locations while waiting for trucks to transport it.

Komboli says the additional vehicles will help his team collect and remove rubbish from different locations more efficiently, improving waste management and keeping Goroka clean.

The dedication ceremony was witnessed by Goroka MP Aiye Tambua, provincial government officials and GULLG staff.

With demand for services continuing to grow, Abori is also calling on all district MPs to support the LLG, saying the responsibility of maintaining Goroka as the province’s central town should not rest solely with the Goroka MP.

item.title: Hagen market security to be tightened
item.description: Police in Western Highlands are calling for stronger security measures at Mt Hagen Main Market, as the market prepares to reopen following its recent closure. Provincial Police Commander Chief Superintendent John Sagom says security must be treated as a top priority to protect market vendors, customers and businesses operating in and around the facility.
item.content:encoded:
Police in Western Highlands are calling for stronger security measures at Mt Hagen Main Market, as the market prepares to reopen following its recent closure.

Provincial Police Commander Chief Superintendent John Sagom says security must be treated as a top priority to protect market vendors, customers and businesses operating in and around the facility.

Chief Superintendent Sagom has outlined a number of security measures to the Hagen Market Board and management in a meeting earlier this week, saying strict controls will be needed to maintain order and prevent criminal activities.

He also says police have agreed with the market management to strengthen the security presence by deploying police reservists and Mobile Squad personnel to the market area.

Sagom adds access into the main market should also be reduced, with only three or four gates kept open.

He says this will allow police to better control and monitor people entering and leaving the market.

Another key measure is a ban on knives and other sharp objects inside the market.

Police are expected to search people entering through the gates, market vendors will also be required to comply with the restriction.

"While police and councillors are carrying out security checks inside the market area for knife or any dangerous objects, those sellers who sells goods like pineapple and sugarcane, will also be required not to carry or use their knives in the market.

"This is to make sure that when a fight or quarrel sparks in the market, this objects are not easily accessible," Sagom stressed.

Sagom is also calling for a holding cell to be established within the market premises.

He says people caught breaching market rules could be held there while awaiting court appearances and prosecution.

The police commander reiterates that the so-called “market taxis” or market helpers should also not be allowed inside the market.

He says the sale of illegal drugs must be strictly prohibited, with people entering the market thoroughly checked.

Sagom has also proposed the establishment of a permanent police post inside the market and the installation of CCTV cameras across the market premises.

He says while the measures may appear extensive, they are necessary to protect the welfare and safety of everyone using the market.

Sagom elaborates the recent closure of the Hagen Market affected everyone, including vendors, farmers, customers and business houses, but there was little they could do other than wait for the market to reopen.

He is now appealing to the market management to strictly enforce city rules and regulations.

Sagom adds management must not fear or favour anyone with an interest in the market, stressing that the safety and welfare of the public must come first.

item.title: Fuel price to increase starting this Sunday
item.description: Fuel prices for November will increase from the October subsidized price. This following the cessation of the Government's fuel relief assistance.
item.content:encoded:
Fuel prices for November will increase from the October subsidized price.

This following the cessation of the Government's fuel relief assistance.

The government has now removed its one-billion-kina fuel relief assistance, reprioritizing funding for El Nino dry conditions severely affecting the country.

Independent Consumer and Competition Commission highlighted says this will see the increase of fuel products for this month, that will come into effect on Sunday the 8th of November.

Petrol is expected to increase by about 30 toea from k5.90 and will sell at K6.19 per liter, diesel will increase by 79 toea from K5.90 and will sell at K6.69 whilst kerosene sells at K6.57 an increase of about 67 toea from K5.90

The impact of the increase will be partially offset by the Government's fuel relief assistance through the continued exemption of Goods and Services Tax (GST) on fuel prices, thus the increase in toeas.

ICCC highlights this, few days ahead of the implementation date.

item.title: ICCC monitors prices of rice, flour and sugar
item.description: The independent Consumer and Competition Commission will continue to check prices of rice, flour and sugar to make sure businesses are not over pricing, and consumers are not exploited or cheated by paying more. This follows the global price increases of the three basic items.
item.content:encoded:
The independent Consumer and Competition Commission will continue to check prices of rice, flour and sugar to make sure businesses are not over pricing, and consumers are not exploited or cheated by paying more.

This follows the global price increases of the three basic items.

ICCC in a Public notice says these three markets are competitive, however some big suppliers may have strong influence over prices, and when they increase their prices, other businesses may follow.

Papua New Guinea is an import-dependent economy and is exposed to changes in global food and fuel prices.

According to Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) data, prices for rice, flour, and sugar have all increased in September 2026 due to dry El Nino conditions, disruptions in ship routes, high fuel costs due to the Middle east war and continued depreciation PNG Kina value.

Rice prices in Vietnam and Thailand have increased by 10 to 13 percent in 2026, while international sugar prices rose by 14.7 percent over the past year. Wheat prices also increased by 30 percent this year.

In light of these factors, ICCC warns that consumer prices in the country are likely to remain high for some time into 2027.

Businesses may use this opportunity to increase prices unfairly, thus the need for ICCC to continue monitoring this to make sure businesses do not work together to increase prices unfairly and that consumers are not exploited.

These are three basic items declared under the Prices Regulation Act for price monitoring purposes only.

ICCC explains that monitoring does not mean prices are fixed or controlled, as retailers remain free to set their own prices.

However, pricing decisions must be made independently and must comply with applicable competition laws.

The consumer watchdog monitors the factory -gate and retail prices of rice, flour and sugar, this helps assess whether price movements are consistent with changes in global prices, kina exchange rate and shipping and fuel costs.

This helps ICCC identify any conduct by suppliers, wholesalers and retailers that may exploit consumers or abuse kina power.

It says it will investigate unusual pricing patterns and take action where businesses are found to be engaging in anti-competitive practices.

Meantime, the Commission has also reminded the public that it does not regulate the prices of all goods and services in the country, but only those specifically declared under the relevant laws.

item.content:encoded:
Education Minister Francis Siune presented a K5 million dummy cheque to Hela province yesterday to boost Flexible Open Distance Education (FODE) infrastructure across the province.

Under the funding package, Hela's four districts — Koroba-Lake Kopiago, Magarima, Komo-Hulia and Tari-Pori — will each receive K1 million to upgrade their FODE facilities. The remaining K1 million has been allocated to the Pai Hope Institute for the construction of a new Information and Communication Technology (ICT) laboratory.

Minister Siune was with delegation including Education Secretary Dr. Uke Kombra, FODE Principal Anthony Rayapen, First Assistant Secretary for FODE and Inclusive Education Andrew Angobe, and First Assistant Secretary for Projects and Procurement Malon Acquino. Joined by Hela Governor Philip Undialu, the Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu and other distinguished guests.

Commending Governor Undialu's administration for making distance learning a provincial priority, Minister Siune linked the educational investment directly to provincial peace efforts, noting that the ongoing gun surrender program provides a vital opening for transformation.

"Hela should be competing in education, business and other meaningful pursuits — not violence and tribal conflict," Minister Siune said. "When Hiroshima and Nagasaki were bombed by the US during the Second World War, Japan did not retaliate with arms; it focused on becoming a prosperous nation. That is the exact path Hela must take."

He emphasized that the Marape-Rosso Government remains focused on creating second-chance pathways for school dropouts and students unable to secure tertiary placements and is giving priority to supporting FODE across the country.

Governor Undialu supported the Minister's message, urging parents, guardians and community leaders to actively encourage out-of-school youth and school leavers to enroll at FODE and TVET institutions.

"The Government is building the pathways. There is no longer any excuse for a student in Hela to be left behind," Governor Undialu said.
